The Torah source text is extremely brief — a single paragraph of approximately 60 Hebrew words. It contains one explicit bechina statement: 'שֶׁהָיוּ נוֹשְׂאִין בַּכָּתֵף אֶת הָאָרוֹן, הַיְנוּ בְּחִינַת עֹל תּוֹרָה' — carrying the Ark on the shoulder is the bechina of the yoke of Torah.

The Torah's argument is a single conceptual move: (1) Melody is a sign of accepting the yoke of Torah. (2) Proof: the word 'ישָׂאוּ' (carry/bear) means both physical carrying AND song (per the Sages, Arakhin 11), as in 'שְׂאוּ זִמְרָה.' (3) This verse was said about the Kehat family carrying the Ark on their shoulders, which is explicitly called 'the bechina of the yoke of Torah.'

The implicit chain: נגינה / שירה ≈ נשיאה בכתף ≈ עול תורה. These three are all expressions of the same essential act of accepting and bearing the holy burden. The primary bechina pair that should be entered in the dataset is: כָּתֵף (shoulder-bearing) ↔ עֹל תּוֹרָה (yoke of Torah), with the supporting bechina שִׁירָה ↔ נשיאה (song ↔ carrying), making melody = carrying = yoke of Torah a three-node chain.

Polarity: The entire Torah is oriented toward the good domain. There is no evil mirror in this teaching — it does not discuss an opposition force or negative counterpart to melody or Torah acceptance. This is a pure positive teaching about how melody reveals Torah-acceptance.
